content:
The image shows a mango leaf with:
- Grayish-white powdery patches scattered across the leaf surface
- The coating appears dusty/mealy in texture
- The leaf is otherwise intact (no necrosis, no lesions with dark borders, no die-back of the tip, no black sooty coating)
- The distribution is diffuse across the blade, not concentrated at margins or tips

Matching against classes:
- **Anthracnose**: dark/brown necrotic lesions with defined margins — not present
- **Die_Back**: tip/margin necrosis progressing inward — not present
- **Powdery_Mildew**: white-gray powdery coating on leaf surface — matches well
- **Sooty_Mould**: black sooty coating, usually on upper surface — not present (coloring is gray-white, not black)

The diffuse grayish-white powdery patches are characteristic of Powdery Mildew infection.
